items.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Resample synthetic rejections from the target distribution
items.author: cquil11
items.summary: Synthetic acceptance rejects drafts with a seeded coin flip, not a p/q test, but the rejected slot is still resampled from max(p - q, 0). That residual is only the right conditional after a real rejection.
items.body:
Synthetic acceptance rejects drafts with a seeded coin flip, not a p/q test, but the rejected slot is still resampled from max(p - q, 0). That residual is only the right conditional after a real rejection. Under synthetic acceptance it drops the mass the draft agrees with and over-samples tokens the draft under-weights, such as channel and tool delimiters, which strict tool parsers then turn into empty responses.

This resamples the rejected slot from the target distribution when synthetic acceptance is enabled. Acceptance timing is unchanged, and non-synthetic paths are untouched.

items.author: Pb314314
items.summary: Fixes incorrect video timestamps in MiMo-V2 omni by preserving loader metadata and computing timestamps from actual sampled frame times instead of assuming 1 fps.

### What

Fixes #65523.

is labelled `00:00, 00:02, …, 00:30` regardless of its real length. The model then reports
wrong timestamps and slices long videos at wrong positions.

Original authors: @yhyang201, @Oasis-Git

## Port of #48414

Under DCP, the Kimi-K3.1 Day-0 branch (#48414) shards the DSA indexer's index-K cache by token: each rank selects a local top-k and the ranks merge them into the global top-k. This PR ports the merge for decode rows: one kernel that exchanges candidates over NVLink multicast and selects the global top-k exactly. It comes with a test and has no caller yet.

items.author: grYe99
items.summary: Adds opt-in cross-layer sharing of the lightning-indexer top-k selection to the NVIDIA MiniMax-M3 path, porting #47269 (AMD-only until now). When is set, only 1 of every sparse-attention layers recomputes the indexer score + top-k; the rest reuse the selection…
items.body:
## Summary

Adds opt-in **cross-layer sharing** of the lightning-indexer top-k selection to the NVIDIA MiniMax-M3 path, porting #47269 (AMD-only until now). When `use_index_cache` is set, only 1 of every `index_topk_freq` sparse-attention layers recomputes the indexer score + top-k; the rest reuse the selection the preceding compute layer wrote into the shared `topk_indices_buffer` in the same forward pass.

Adjacent sparse layers pick nearly the same blocks, so this cuts the indexer cost ~`freq`×. The skip decision is computed once per layer at construction (static → cudagraph-capture-safe).

items.title: [Bugfix][Attention] Prevent overlapping query tile writes in Triton unified attention
items.author: shiwanhang6868-arch
items.summary: Fixes overlapping query-tile writes in vLLM's Triton unified attention kernel when GQA ratio is not a power of two, where padding rows incorrectly access queries owned by adjacent tiles.
items.body:
Overview

This PR fixes overlapping query-tile reads and writes in vLLM's Triton unified attention kernel when the GQA ratio is not a power of two.

The current query mask checks whether a query position is within the entire request, but does not ensure that the row belongs to the current query tile. As a result, padding rows can access queries owned by the next tile, potentially causing overlapping writes to attention outputs and split-K scratch buffers.

This PR intro

items.author: shuoerw
items.summary: Static EPLB dispatch-map construction computes assignments for all EP ranks, then returns only the current rank's map. It also repeatedly converts individual candidate tensors to Python lists and scans replica candidates for each rank.
items.body:
## Motivation

Static EPLB dispatch-map construction computes assignments for all EP ranks, then returns only the current rank's map. It also repeatedly converts individual candidate tensors to Python lists and scans replica candidates for each rank.

Reduce this CPU overhead while preserving dispatch decisions.

## Modifications

- Convert the candidate tensor to Python lists once.
- Index candidate replicas by GPU and node while preserving candidate order.
- Construct only the current rank's output map.
- Preserve nearest-replica selection, remote-rank ordering, and seeded fair-choice calls.

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

With speculative decoding (MTP), an eager decode-only step pads its request

than the step's token buffers, and the forward fails in
`apply_rotary_emb_key()`.

items.title: [Bugfix][MiniMax-M3] Initialize the shard record in the indexer QKV layer
items.author: gau-nernst
items.summary: Fixes MiniMax-M3 checkpoint loading failure by initializing `loaded_shard_ids` via `StackedColumnParallelLinear.__init__` in the custom QKV indexer layer.
items.body:
## Purpose

Since #63752, MiniMax-M3 checkpoints fail to load:

```
AttributeError: 'MinimaxM3QKVParallelLinearWithIndexer' object has no attribute 'loaded_shard_ids'
```

#63752 added the per-shard loading record (`loaded_shard_ids`) in
`StackedColumnParallelLinear.__init__`. `MinimaxM3QKVParallelLinearWithIndexer` skips
`QKVParallelLinear.__init__` (it builds its own 5-group layout) by calling
`ColumnParallelLinear.__init__` directly, so it skipped the stacked init too.

Call `StackedColumnParallelLinear.__init__` instead. It sets up the record and forwards to
`ColumnParallelLinear.__init__`

## Motivation

Under overload, the existing policies trade fairness for work differently, and none gives a wait bound. `fcfs` bounds waits but ignores work; `lpm` and `shortest-prefill-first` favor cheap requests and can starve large ones; `hrrn` ages by waited tokens. On agentic workloads (long shared contexts, heavy-tailed outputs) we see a long TTFT tail of requests that wait minutes.

UniBoost (*Beyond Prediction: Tail-Aware Scheduling for LLM Inference*, ICML 2026, https://yl3469.github.io/uniboost-icml26/#cite) is a prediction-free policy with one knob. Requests are served in ascending `

## Overview

On Hopper with DeepGEMM installed, `is_deep_gemm_e8m0_used()` is true by default for every layer. This forces two costs on the Triton FP8 MoE path, which takes float32 scales:

- **Power-of-two activation scales.** It rounds both of its activation quants' scales to powers of two, which adds error and buys nothing.
- **Unfused SiLU+quant.** It skips the fused `silu_and_mul_per_block_quant`, so SiLU+Mul and quant run as two kernels.

This PR makes the scale format a per-layer property of the selected MoE backend, and runs the fused kernel in every case

items.body:
## Motivation

An external multimodal processor built on the Rust frontend (`MmProcessor`) has two blind spots. It cannot report Prometheus metrics of its own: the frontend writes its families to the multiprocess directory that `/metrics` merges, but an extension's counters and histograms have no way in. And it cannot see how admission handled a request's media before `process` runs: how long the prefetch took, which sources its own `fetch_media` resolved and how long each took, or when the request was queued for an MM worker. Both are needed for a processor to report per-request media timing

items.body:
## Overview

When a tool-call message arrives in one streamed delta, ernie45 emits only the first call, while jamba and granite-20b-fc emit none or mangle the calls. This change makes each parser emit every call completed by a delta. Fixes #48294.

## Claims

- All three parsers emit every tool call completed in a single delta (async scheduling, `stream_interval > 1`) instead of dropping or mangling calls.

- ernie45 streaming no longer leaks text between tool calls into content; leading/trailing

items.title: [Fix] deepseek_v4: floor amax before the division in the V4.1 fp8 KV scale
items.author: howl9003
items.summary: The V4.1 fp8 KV store and its pure-torch reference floor the scale quotient,, so the smallest scale is 2^-13. DeepSeek's floors first,, so its smallest scale is 2^-22.
items.body:
## Motivation

The V4.1 fp8 KV store (`store_row_fp8`) and its pure-torch reference floor the scale quotient, `2^ceil(log2(max(amax / 448, 1e-4)))`, so the smallest scale is 2^-13. DeepSeek's `act_quant` (`scale_fmt="ue8m0"`) floors `amax` first, `max(amax, 1e-4) / 448`, so its smallest scale is 2^-22. Every 32-value tile with `amax <= 448 * 2^-14` (about 0.027) gets a coarser scale than the reference. The reference had the same error, so the byte-exact store test could not catch it.

## Modifications

- `kv_layout.cuh`: exponent floor 114 -> 105 (2^-13 -> 2^-22). Shared by the CUDA and HIP bu

items.title: [Core] Cheapen the spin while waiting for model output
items.author: njhill
items.summary: This delays the engine's input and output threads, and costs some throughput and tail latency, even when no inputs are handled during the wait. Between polls, spin directly on the response queue's flags and the input queue instead, so that an iteration costs a…
items.body:
#65466 waits for a step's output by looping on future.poll(), which runs several Python calls with the GIL held before each sched_yield(). This delays the engine's input and output threads, and costs some throughput and tail latency, even when no inputs are handled during the wait.

Between polls, spin directly on the response queue's flags and the input queue instead, so that an iteration costs about 1us rather than 4us. Inputs are still handled as they arrive, so requests still reach the scheduler about as early as with #65466 (median queue wait about 25us, compared with 5-7ms before it).

Two Kimi-K3 request shapes are handled differently from the Kimi-K3 API:

items.summary: We run SGLang's in-process (no tokenizer/detokenizer subprocesses), on every TP rank, driven by an outer loop that adds requests, steps the scheduler once, and collects results between steps (an RL rollout service that also loads new weights between steps). / …
items.body:
We run SGLang's `Scheduler` in-process (no tokenizer/detokenizer subprocesses), on every TP rank, driven by an outer loop that adds requests, steps the scheduler once, and collects results between steps (an RL rollout service that also loads new weights between steps). `Scheduler.run_event_loop` / `event_loop_overlap` / `event_loop_normal` only run forever, so we copy their loop bodies into our own `step()`. The copy uses private members (`_apply_war_barrier`, `_sched_idled`, `_war_barrier_enabled`, `result_queue`, the schedule-stream context) and must be re-synced on every SGLang bump.

items.author: BBuf
items.summary: Tuned Triton MoE TMA kernel configs for LingBot-Video 30B-A3B on B300 SXM6, enabling optimized up/down projection paths for the ~33k-token expert input region.
items.body:
LingBot-Video MoE 30B-A3B uses the untuned MoE heuristic on NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC. At 832 × 480 × 81, its approximately 33k-token expert inputs spend 39% of summed GPU kernel time in MoE. This enables the existing up/down TMA paths for that region using the existing tile sizes.

Two Triton 3.8.0 configs target E=128/N=768 on this exact device name. Only the 32768-token bin uses TMA; nearest-bin lookup selects it for integer M=24577…49152. Other bins preserve the native heuristic. Since the config key omits hidden size, the up projection falls back when an outer weight stride is not 16-byte align

items.author: Fridge003
items.summary: Kimi-K3.1 PCP currently replicates persistent DSA KV across ranks. Store each logical KV page and packed index page on its owner rank, then assemble the working prefix for TRTLLM DSA attention.
items.body:
## Motivation

Kimi-K3.1 PCP currently replicates persistent DSA KV across ranks. Store each logical KV page and packed index page on its owner rank, then assemble the working prefix for TRTLLM DSA attention. This extends the existing page-sharded KV infrastructure to Kimi's hybrid attention, HiCache L2 and DFlash paths.

This PR targets `kimi-k3.1-day-0`, the branch of #48414.

## Modifications

- Add `--kv-cache-sharding-scratch-size` (GiB per GPU, default 10) to bound the two prefix-assembly buffers. Account for active prefixes, overlap and verification headroom in admission and retraction.

items.author: jcotant-inferact
items.summary: Every new model iteration requires new label automation, which has become diminishing returns. This consolidates labeling onto vendor/family labels (matching what SGLang does for new-model tracking): - Drop the / rules — mentions in titles now fold into the ve…
items.body:
## Purpose

The repo currently tracks a mix of vendor/family labels (`deepseek`, `qwen`, `minimax`, `kimi`, …) and per-model-version labels (`DSv4`, `DSv4.1`, `k3`, `Qwen3.5+`). Every new model iteration requires new label automation, which has become diminishing returns. This consolidates labeling onto vendor/family labels (matching what SGLang does for new-model tracking):

- **Drop the `DSv4` / `DSv4.1` rules** — `DSv4` mentions in titles now fold into the `deepseek` vendor label. The existing `deepseek` file rules already cover the `vllm/models/deepseek_v4*/` trees, so no coverage is lost.

items.title: [Fix] disaggregation: Publish a yielded optimistic prefill's KV under a write-through cache
items.author: metamergebot
items.summary: Fixes a bug where yielded optimistic prefill requests skip KV checkpointing under write-through HiCache, causing redundant recomputation on retry instead of L3 lookup.
items.body:
## Motivation

An optimistic prefill request yields when its prefill finishes before its decode peer has bootstrapped: the scheduler releases its KV and requeues it for a retry. `optimistic_release_and_requeue` checkpoints the KV the request computed into the radix tree before the release, so the retry matches that prefix instead of recomputing it.

Under a write-through HiCache that checkpoint was skipped. Pending-bootstrap KV is kept request-owned under write-through (#38978) so that the decode bootstrap path never waits on a host/L3 backup, and the release path inherited the same condition.

items.title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Use the single-kernel DSv4 top-k on ROCm
items.author: davzhuAMD
items.summary: On ROCm, DeepSeek-V4/V4.1's sqrtsoftplus routing never reaches vLLM's single-launch Triton top-k, because requires; it runs the generic HIP kernel instead. This PR allows on ROCm, and also calls it from the AITER fused-MoE branch of, the branch the DSv4.1 ROCm…
items.body:
## Overview

On ROCm, DeepSeek-V4/V4.1's sqrtsoftplus routing never reaches vLLM's single-launch Triton top-k (`dsv4_topk`), because `can_use_dsv4_topk()` requires `current_platform.is_cuda()`; it runs the generic HIP `topkGatingSoftplusSqrt` kernel instead. ## Overview

Adaptive verification (AV) caps its per-step draft budget so that all verified logits fit in one rejection-sampling chunk: 2^30 / (vocab × 4) rows, which is 2,076 rows for a 129k vocab and 1,081 rows for a 248k vocab. items.author: Pb314314
items.summary: Fixes 32-bit integer overflow in persistent and cooperative top-k kernels that caused wrong row selections when logits exceeded 2^32 elements.

`persistent_topk` and `cooperative_topk` compute each row's start in the logits tensor as a 32-bit product. items.title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] gdn: deferred-fold ReplaySSM target verify on FlashInfer u-cache kernels
items.author: ameynaik-hub
items.summary: With a bf16 SSM state, folds the GDN state on every verify step. passes, so the cursor kernel marks every row that accepted a token as "flush".
items.body:
## Motivation

With a bf16 SSM state, `--enable-linear-replayssm-spec` folds the GDN state on every verify step. `spec_utils.py` passes `fold_every_commit = temporal.dtype != torch.float32`, so the cursor kernel marks every row that accepted a token as "flush". The ring never carries history across steps, and one all-layer commit kernel reads and writes the full recurrent state every step. On B200 (TP1, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4, NEXTN 3/4) that commit costs 2.3 / 4.7 / 10.2 / 21 ms per decode step at B = 64 / 128 / 256 / 512.

This PR adds a separate, **off-by-default** GDN target-verify path

items.author: yanzi-elastix

items.body:
## Overview

The CPU Gated DeltaNet decode kernel computes the gate `beta = sigmoid(b)` in bf16, while the CPU spec-decode kernel and the Triton GPU kernel compute it in float32. So plain decode and speculative verification of the same token feed different `beta` into the state update, and greedy speculative decoding on CPU cannot reproduce greedy plain decoding. This PR computes `beta` in float32 in the decode kernel, as the other two already do.

In Kimi-K3's MoE (E = 896, top-16, block_m 32), small batches go through a patched sort kernel that also quantizes the stage-1 input to MXFP8. Until now it covered at most 256 (token, expert) pairs, i.e. 16 tokens at top-16; larger batches fell back to aiter's opus sort + quant.

items.author: micmelesse
items.summary: Adds a custom ROCm communicator that fuses all-reduce with downstream ops (AttnRes, RMSNorm) into single kernels, reducing launch overhead and improving Kimi-K3 inference throughput by 1.9–5.4%.
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This PR adds `HipCustomCommunicator`, a communicator for ROCm on gfx950 that uses our own HIP kernels. It is built for complex fusions. The op after the all-reduce runs in the same kernel. This saves that op's launch and its re-read of the sum.

The first complex fusion is AttnRes. AttnRes updates the prefix, takes a softmax over the earlier blocks, and applies an RMSNorm. The communicator also fuses the all-reduce with RMSNorm, and runs the plain all-reduce. More complex fusions follow in later PRs. A tuned table picks each call's config by sh

## Motivation

Two AITER fp8 prefill paths read K and V back from the cache, but cast q to fp8 without scaling it and pass the layer's `k_scale` as q's descale:

- the gfx950 head-dim-256 context-chunk prefill (the ASM varlen kernel over the gathered NHD cache).

items.title: [Perf][KV Connector] Mooncake store: build and parse lookup candidates in bulk
items.author: gcanlin
items.summary: runs on the worker process (the thread). With fine-grained prefix hits it builds and parses one candidate key per hash unit per KV cache group in per-key Python loops, holding the GIL that the worker's main thread needs to launch the forward pass.
items.body:
## Overview

`MooncakeStoreWorker.lookup` runs on the worker process (the `LookupKeyServer` thread). With fine-grained prefix hits it builds and parses one candidate key per hash unit per KV cache group in per-key Python loops, holding the GIL that the worker's main thread needs to launch the forward pass. This PR builds the candidates and evaluates the results in bulk; the keys sent to `batch_is_exist` (in order) and the resulting exists set are unchanged.

## Claims

- Lookup CPU time is 3.5x lower at the same candidate keys. For a 100K-token prompt (31K keys), it drops from 42.3 ms to 12.

items.title: [Fix] deterministic: Size the MQA-logits chunks without free memory
items.author: aarnetalman
items.summary: The sparse-attention indexers (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5, DeepSeek-V4) split their MQA-logits matrix into row chunks, and sizes the chunks from the free GPU memory at that moment. Free memory changes from run to run, so the chunking does too, and the logits kernel'…
items.body:
## Motivation

The sparse-attention indexers (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5, DeepSeek-V4) split their MQA-logits matrix into row chunks, and `mqa_logits_budget_bytes` sizes the chunks from the free GPU memory at that moment. Free memory changes from run to run, so the chunking does too, and the logits kernel's result for a row depends on the chunk size. With `--enable-deterministic-inference`, the same prompt can then give different tokens from run to run when the server is short of free memory: GLM-5.3-Flash at TP2 with `--mem-fraction-static 0.9` did, with a 32k-token prompt sent twice on its own.

items.title: [Bug] MiniMax M2 streaming parser loses buffered text at finish
items.author: 0z5a
items.summary: After parsing a complete block, it retains trailing text in, but inherits a no-op. Text ending in a partial prefix can be held the same way.
items.body:
## Bug

`MiniMaxM2ToolParser` can silently drop ordinary text at the end of a streaming response. After parsing a complete `</minimax:tool_call>` block, it retains trailing text in `_buffer`, but inherits a no-op `finish()`. Text ending in a partial `<minimax:tool_call>` prefix can be held the same way.

## Reproduction

On main `a32d6660`, pass one increment containing:

```text
<minimax:tool_call><invoke name="clock"></invoke></minimax:tool_call>suffix
```

`parse_streaming_increment` emits the tool call but no ordinary text, and `finish()` emits nothing even though `suffix` remains buffered

items.title: [Fix] diffusion: Count reclaimable page cache as available inside a cgroup cap
items.author: mickqian
items.summary: Inside a memory-capped cgroup, took the cgroup's as used. That number includes the page cache charged to the cgroup, which the kernel reclaims under the cap.
items.body:
## Motivation

Inside a memory-capped cgroup, `physical_host_memory_available_bytes()` took the cgroup's `memory.current` as used. That number includes the page cache charged to the cgroup, which the kernel reclaims under the cap. Outside a cgroup the same function uses psutil's `available` (MemAvailable), which counts that cache as available. So the two paths disagreed.

Seen on an RTX 5090 desktop with 60 GB RAM, MiniMax-H3 T2VA 480p, run in `systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=56G` right after another engine ran in the same scope:

| | host memory log | DiT layers pinned | denoise |
|--

## Motivation

For Kimi K3, usage leaves the three-token assistant generation stub out of `prompt_tokens` (`_reported_prompt_tokens`), but `cached_tokens` is reported as the engine counted it. The stub is model input, so a prefix-cache hit on the whole prompt covers it, and usage can report more cached tokens than prompt tokens, for example `prompt_tokens: 1022` with `cached_tokens: 1024`. Anything that computes uncached input as `prompt_tokens - cached_tokens` then gets a negative number; we hit this in a billing pipeline that rejected the usage of every full-prompt cache hit.

#35863 fix

## Overview

With pipeline parallelism, each step's intermediate tensors go from one stage to the next over NCCL send / recv. On ROCm that peer copy runs as a blit kernel on the sender's CUs, so it slows whatever the sender computes next to it: an 8192^3 bf16 GEMM on the sender runs 5.1x slower while a 201 MiB tensor is copied to the next GPU (table below). In a TP1 x PP2 prefill of MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, a 16384-token step hands off several such tensors on both stages' compute path.

## Summary

Extend the chunked optimizer offload introduced in #6244 to stage MCore-owned FP32 master parameters together with optimizer state.

Previously, selected MCore masters were restored to CUDA as a full window, limiting peak-memory savings. This change updates whole parameter matrices in bounded chunks and copies updated BF16 weights back before offloading each chunk.

- Use CUDA gradient proxies for gradient statistics and clipping.
- Add optional three-buffer

items.title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Refresh streaming request keys after preemption
items.author: waizuichougou
items.summary: With lookahead block hashing, a streaming input continuation can replace a token included in a cached block's hash. If the request is preempted, the scheduler recomputes its block hashes from the current tokens, but retains its previously recorded keys.
items.body:
## Overview

With lookahead block hashing, a streaming input continuation can replace a token included in a cached block's hash. If the request is preempted, the scheduler recomputes its block hashes from the current tokens, but `OffloadingConnector` retains its previously recorded keys. It can then look up stale entries or skip storing the recomputed KV, causing later requests to miss the CPU cache and recompute the prefix.

Before looking up a resumed request, refresh each group's offload keys against the recomputed hashes. Preserve the unchanged prefix and rebuild only the changed suffix.

items.author: BugenZhao

items.body:
## Overview

OpenAI's chat API allows a `refusal` content part in assistant messages (`ChatCompletionContentPartRefusalParam`; the assistant `content` array is `text | refusal`), so a client that replays a model's refusal as structured history sends it. The Python frontend accepts it and replays the refusal string as text. The Rust frontend rejects the whole request at deserialization (`unknown variant 'refusal'`), because `ContentPart` only knows `text`, the three media URLs and `input_audio`.

This PR adds `ContentPart::Refusal` and lowers it where the role is known.

Allow explicitly declared private fixed-state groups to activate after request admission and release their slots during suspension. Allocation failure preserves the previous activation selection. `None` on resume retains that selection; an explicit empty list selects only initially active groups. Sizing descriptors use the same selection as allocation.

items.title: Add an optional TensorAtomic placement for MCore MFSDP v2 dense parameters
items.author: Autumn1998
items.summary: Muon needs each weight matrix whole on one rank to run Newton-Schulz. MFSDP v2 shards the matrices, so today the optimizer step gathers each matrix's pieces to an owner rank and scatters the update back.
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Muon needs each weight matrix whole on one rank to run Newton-Schulz. MFSDP v2 shards the matrices, so today the optimizer step gathers each matrix's pieces to an owner rank and scatters the update back. This PR adds an optional alternative: with `MFSDP_TENSOR_ATOMIC=1`, every dense parameter stays whole on one owner rank (the `TensorAtomic` placement), so the Muon step needs no gather or scatter. Owners are chosen greedily to balance the Newton-Schulz cost. The plan depends only on parameter shapes, so every rank computes the same one. Experts keep their own mesh.

items.title: [ray] fix: prevent master port races during worker startup
items.author: SeptPonts
items.summary: Prevent during Ray worker startup caused by the gap between selecting a master port and binding PyTorch's TCPStore. Previously, probed a free port with a temporary socket, closed it, and passed the port to workers.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Prevent `EADDRINUSE` during Ray worker startup caused by the gap between selecting a master port and binding PyTorch's TCPStore.

Previously, `RayWorkerGroup` probed a free port with a temporary socket, closed it, and passed the port to workers. Another process could claim that port before rank zero initialized its process group.

Rank zero now binds and retains the actual TCPStore before invoking the user worker constructor. It publishes the bound endpoint before that constructor can block waiting for peers, allowing the driver to start the remaining ranks.

## Description

`setup.py` now hard-links the package files when it builds the wheel, instead of letting setuptools copy them. The wheel is the same. The build is faster and puts less load on the filesystem metadata server.

Before this PR, `python -m build --wheel` copied the whole package twice before it zipped it. `build_py` copied `tensorrt_llm/` and the other packages into `build/lib.<platform>/`. Then `install_lib` copied `build/lib.<platform>/` into `build/bdist.<platform>/wheel/`, which `bdist_wheel` zips and then deletes. For a built checkout that is 2.4 GB in 13,207 files, each time.

items.title: Fix math_dapo Minerva extraction for markdown-decorated answers
items.author: siddhant-rajhans
items.summary: The existing regex captures the markers as part of the answer, so correct answers score -1.0. Fixes #8449 ## Root cause The Minerva answer pattern matches the literal "Answer" and captures everything after the colon to end of line.
items.body:
## Bug

Models commonly wrap the Minerva `Answer:` label in markdown bold/italic (`**Answer:** 42`, `Answer: **42**`, `**Answer:**\n\n42`). The existing regex captures the `*` markers as part of the answer, so correct answers score -1.0.

Fixes #8449

## Root cause

The Minerva answer pattern `(?i)Answer\s*:\s*([^\n]+)` matches the literal "Answer" and captures everything after the colon to end of line. When models decorate with markdown:

| Input | Extracted | After normalize | Score |
|---|---|---|---|
| `**Answer:** 42` | `** 42` | `**42` | -1.0 |
| `Answer: **42**` | `**42**` | `**42**` |

- The result is a deadlock until the NCCL timeout, or a later WORLD collective pair

## Problem

For `k3` and `low_var_kl`, `compute_approx_kl` evaluates `exp(x) - 1 - x`, where `x = log_probs_base - log_probs`. This expression is nonnegative in real arithmetic, but subtracting 1 from a float32 exponential can erase the small KL term or make it negative when the policies are close.

With valid finite log-probabilities near -0.1, I reproduced a value of -1.4901161e-8 where an 80-digit reference gives 4.9986626e-11. The helper feeds the reported KL term and configured KL loss/reward paths; the Search-R1 example selects `low_var_kl` with a nonzero KL-loss coefficient.

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8433.

`SFTTrainer` built its train/val `StatefulDataLoader`s without a `generator`, so every iterator construction drew a `base_seed` from the global CPU RNG. On resume that draw happens right after the checkpoint manager restores `torch.get_rng_state()`, so the resumed run continued from a different global CPU RNG state than an uninterrupted run. This PR gives each dataloader its own seeded `torch.Generator`, so building iterators no longer touches the global CPU RNG and the restored state is the one training actually continues with.

items.title: fix: retain GPU locks while canceling command groups
items.author: bvolpato
items.summary: Signal the whole owned command group on cancellation and retain GPU locks during bounded cleanup.
items.body:
## Summary

Signal the whole owned command group on cancellation and retain GPU locks during bounded cleanup.

### Motivation

The cancellation handler stops only the direct child and exits as soon as that child finishes. A worker descendant can continue running after the launcher releases its GPU locks, allowing a later command to acquire the same lock and overlap the canceled work. With `--partial-rollout`, a sample aborted mid-generation goes back to the data buffer and is resumed later. `generate()` resumes it with a `max_new_tokens` budget reduced by `sample.response_length` and appends the new tokens after the existing response, so the request must be conditioned on that response.

### What does this PR do?

Adds `sharded_nixl`, a checkpoint engine for disaggregated rollout with no trainer-side all-gather. Every trainer rank (FSDP or Megatron) exports only the shards it holds and NIXL-WRITEs them into the rollout workers' staging buffers. When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. This RFC proposes how to land Ascend NPU support in vime `main`. A few places in the core assume CUDA; this proposal turns them into hardware-neutral extension points on `Accelerator`. items.title: fix(ppo): mask env/tool tokens out of the reward KL penalty
items.author: Domin-Focus
items.summary: These tokens are not generated by the policy, but their KL still enters the rewards, and GAE propagates it back into the advantages of the policy tokens before them. This is not only policy/ref drift on env tokens.
items.body:
## Problem

With `--advantage-estimator ppo` and `--kl-coef > 0`, the token-level rewards are built over the whole response (`slime/backends/megatron_utils/loss.py:796`):

```python

```

In multi-turn / agentic rollouts the response includes env/tool tokens with `loss_mask = 0`. These tokens are not generated by the policy, but their KL still enters the rewards, and GAE propagates it back into the advantages of the policy tokens before them.

items.author: Domin-Focus
items.summary: Both are falsy, so the guard treats them as a missing label, and every correct response scores 0 under. Under GRPO, a group where every sample gets 0 gives no learning signal for that prompt.
items.body:
## Problem

`grade_answer_verl` (`slime/rollout/rm_hub/math_utils.py:485`) starts with:

```python
if not ground_truth:
    return False
ground_truth = str(ground_truth)
```

Labels are passed through from the dataset as-is (`slime/utils/data.py:272`), so a zero answer arrives as `0` or `0.0`. Both are falsy, so the guard treats them as a missing label, and every correct `\boxed{0}` response scores 0 under `rm_type=math`. Under GRPO, a group where every sample gets 0 gives no learning signal for that prompt.

items.title: [Bug] Startup health polling can block on an unresponsive server
items.author: LinzeShi
items.summary: If the server accepts the connection but does not respond, startup polling blocks inside that request and cannot reach. This affects VIME's managed vLLM startup wait. [Discussion: independent check on main: this no longer reproduces.]
items.body:
### Bug Description

`_wait_server_healthy()` calls `requests.get(.../health)` without a timeout. If the server accepts the connection but does not respond, startup polling blocks inside that request and cannot reach `is_process_alive()`.

This affects VIME's managed vLLM startup wait. The expected behavior is to bound each probe, then check process liveness and retry while the process is alive. The overall startup wait should remain unbounded for slow model loading.

### Steps to Reproduce

items.title: fix(sglang): validate deployment config before launch
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.
items.body:
## Background

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Problem

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.
- Reject unknown model fields

## Solution

- Register each actor immediately after creation, before rank-0 rendezvous lookup.

items.title: fix(sglang): bound local server startup waits
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.
items.body:
## Background

Locally managed SGLang servers are polled through `/health_generate` before rollout initialization can continue.

## Problem

The startup poll had neither a request timeout nor an overall deadline. A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.

## Solution

- Add `--sglang-server-startup-timeout` with a positive finite value and a conservative 600-second default.
- Use a monotonic deadline and cap every health request by both five seconds and the remaining startup budget.
- Reject readiness

items.title: fix(rollout): support fan-out results in group reward models
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Those paths expect, so fan-out generation and group rewards could not be combined.
items.body:
## Background

A custom generation function may return multiple training segments for one input. `generate_and_rm_group` preserves that result as `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

When `group_rm` is enabled, the nested result was passed directly to the group reward function and trace helper. Those paths expect `list[Sample]`, so fan-out generation and group rewards could not be combined.

## Solution

- Flatten one level before tracing and invoking the group reward function.
- Assign returned rewards to the same leaves in stable fan-out order.
- Preserve the original nested return shape for d

items.title: fix(rollout): handle nested aborted fully-async results
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.
items.body:
## Background

`generate_and_rm_group` supports custom generation that fans one input out into `list[Sample]`, so a fully-async task can return `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

The done callback inspected only the outer list. An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.

## Solution

- Snapshot the flat input group before generation can mutate it.
- Inspect one-level fan-out leaves for `Sample.Status.ABORTED`.
- Requeue the pristine flat snapshot

items.title: fix(rm_hub): stop substring-matching gpqa letter labels and short answers
items.author: shaurya416
items.summary: Fixes #2409 ## Problem falls back to a text match when no option letter can be extracted from the reply. That fallback (1) appended a one-letter gold label as answer text, and (2) searched each candidate as a raw substring of the normalized reply.
items.body:
Fixes #2409

## Problem

`compute_gpqa_reward` falls back to a text match when no option letter can be extracted from the reply. That fallback (1) appended a one-letter gold label as answer text, and (2) searched each candidate as a raw substring of the normalized reply. A reply that never answers, for example `I'm sorry, but I can't help with that.`, therefore scored 1.0 whenever the gold letter (`a`, `b`, `c`) occurred inside a word, and a short numeric choice such as `11` matched inside `2011` or `111`.

## Approach

- A one-character label that is a valid option letter is no longer added t

## Summary

Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path.

Under CUDA autocast, `torch.einsum` can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32. The result is saved for entropy backward, so the precision loss affects both the reported entropy value and its gradient.

This change keeps only that CUDA reduction outside autocast and adds a one-GPU regression suite covering FP16/BF16 autocast, masked/unmasked log-prob paths, metric-only/gradient entropy, and chunked/non-chunked execution.

Fixes #1369.

`distributed_masked_whiten(..., shift_mean=False)` used to center, scale, then add the mean back:

```

items.author: yuyz-cyber
items.summary: When one task raises an exception, the exception is propagated but the unfinished sibling tasks are not cancelled. They can continue generation or reward computation after the rollout has failed, wasting resources and potentially leaving unobserved task except…
items.body:
## Problem

Training and evaluation launch rollout tasks concurrently at three levels: samples within a rollout group, rollout groups within a training batch, and samples within an evaluation batch.

When one task raises an exception, the exception is propagated but the unfinished sibling tasks are not cancelled. They can continue generation or reward computation after the rollout has failed, wasting resources and potentially leaving unobserved task exceptions in the event loop.

## Fix

At each concurrency boundary, cancel unfinished sibling tasks and wait for their cleanup before re-raising

items.author: rootkiller6788
items.summary: Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slimevalidateargs with, because it stat'd args.refload before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.
items.body:
Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slime_validate_args with `TypeError: _path_exists: path should be string, bytes, os.PathLike or integer, not NoneType`, because it stat'd args.ref_load before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.

This adds the same guard: ref_load unset now raises a ValueError telling the user to pass --ref-load, and a ref_load that points nowhere still raises the original FileNotFoundError. Two unit tests cover both cases.

## Problem

`--rollout-temperature 0` is greedy decoding. That is not a usable on-policy RL policy: the sampling distribution is a delta, while log-probs (and PPO ratios) still come from a softmax. Greedy RL should be rejected at config parse, not assumed away in loss code.

`--eval-temperature 0` is unchanged; greedy eval remains valid.

## Change

`slime_validate_args` raises if `rollout_temperature <= 0`.

## Summary

Fix IPv6 URL construction in the vLLM engine control plane.

## Problem

The vLLM subprocess requires an unbracketed IPv6 address when binding
the server, while an IPv6 literal must be enclosed in brackets when
used as the host component of an HTTP URL.

Previously, the health-check path could construct an invalid URL such
as:

`http://2001:db8::1:8000/health`

instead of:

`http://[2001:db8::1]:8000/health`

The health check may then keep retrying failed requests, making engine
startup appear to be stuck.

## Summary

This PR reduces actor-update memory usage when entropy is logged but does not contribute to the loss.

Long-context actor updates can become memory-bound because entropy is evaluated over the full vocabulary. When `entropy_coef == 0`, VIME still computes entropy metrics, but the entropy tensor is only used for reporting and has no gradient contribution. items.summary: Backports vllm-project/vllm#44371 into. Layerwise reload was corrupting unloaded non-persistent buffers during warm weight-sync (surfaced on Gemma, where a buffer drifted 0.0188 → 1.0, spiking trainer↔vLLM KL from 1.52 to 0.008 once fixed).
items.body:
Backports vllm-project/vllm#44371 into `docker/patch/latest/vllm.patch`. Layerwise reload was corrupting unloaded non-persistent buffers during warm weight-sync (surfaced on Gemma, where a `root_size` buffer drifted 0.0188 → 1.0,
spiking trainer↔vLLM KL from 1.52 to 0.008 once fixed). 

Patched against vLLM v0.23.0.

items.author: aoshen02
items.summary: The Qwen3-30B-A3B example page is titled 8xH100, but the first parameter bullet said "in an 8xH800 environment" — an inconsistency inherited from slime. Both are 80 GB cards, so the CPU-Adam rationale is unchanged; this just aligns the text with the page title…
items.body:
The Qwen3-30B-A3B example page is titled **8xH100**, but the first parameter bullet said "in an 8xH800 environment" — an inconsistency inherited from slime. Both are 80 GB cards, so the CPU-Adam rationale is unchanged; this just aligns the text with the page title (zh + en).
